cells.tense: The inner sense of what's fair is here, and it is being acted from.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Something ended or changed this year. Name what it left you — a skill, a person, a way of moving — a few lines, once, and then go on with your day.
cells.core:
You can tell what's fair without running the math. When the road only shows its next step, the sense of what's owed still reads true, and you move on the light you have. Nothing about it is loud. People near you rarely notice it working, and they get the benefit regardless — the arrangement that came out even, the thing you wouldn't do. That steadiness is the thing working well, and nothing here is wrong with it.
Something in the past year ended. The change already happened; this week, before anything new gets decided, take back what it grew. Name what it gave you — a skill, a person, a way of moving — a few lines, once. That's the yield, and it's already yours. Whatever gets weighed next, you'll be walking from that ground instead of toward it.
cells.sheetLine: You can tell what's fair before the road is clear.
cells.place: Where the road shows only its next step.

cells.tense: The fairness check will be run on ground that hasn't been laid yet.
cells.act: hold someone else up with what you have
cells.ask: Someone near you is carrying something heavy. Give one piece of help — your weight under theirs, finished before you leave — and don't wait to be asked.
cells.core:
The compass has started checking choices before they exist. A decision that hasn't arrived is already being judged, and the judging has gotten out past the day it's for. From inside it feels like being careful. What it costs is the ground you're standing on, because the future step is getting read while the present one goes unread — and the present one is the only one with anything in it.
Put the weight down somewhere real. Someone near you is carrying something; give one piece of help you can finish, and finish it before you leave. Not the plan, not the advice. Your weight under theirs. Once the load is held, the checking quiets down for a minute, and whatever it was trying to do gets clearer. One piece, and say nothing about why.
cells.sheetLine: The checking has outrun the day it's for.
cells.place: Where the road shows only its next step.

cells.tense: The compass went quiet some time back, and the road kept its next step to itself.
cells.act: walk the route with someone who is lost on it
cells.ask: Somewhere you've already found your way — a job, a grief, a hard season. Walk that route alongside someone just entering it. Their version, not yours, and they carry it from there.
cells.core:
The inner sense of what's fair has gone quiet, and the road isn't offering even its next step. Decisions get put off until more is known, and more doesn't come. What's undecided sits where you left it, and the price shows up in what doesn't get arranged, what doesn't get said, the door still open behind you. This is not a failure of character. The part of you that reads fairness is running low, and reading this won't fill it.
Fill it from outside. Somewhere you've already found your way — a job, a grief, a hard season. Walk that route alongside someone just entering it. Show it, don't carry them. Saying it aloud is what makes it legible to the one saying it. Their version, not yours, and they take it from there.
cells.sheetLine: You've been waiting for enough light to decide.
cells.place: Where the road shows only its next step.

cells.tense: The compass has been steering and the readings are filed under circumstance.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: On one decision, list the pulls you feel — a few, plainly, no ranking. Mark which are yours. Then act on one today, others left standing where they are.
cells.core:
Several readings of a situation are available to you at once, and one of them already has your hand on it. It arrives as instinct, as a nagging, as what feels off about the plan — and then it gets filed under circumstance or mood. The compass is working. What's missing is any agreement that the readings came from you. Under ambiguity you draw on a fuller set than you'll own up to, and then it reads as the situation.
Put the set where you can see it. Take one decision you're sitting inside, name the pulls you feel — a few, plainly, no ranking — and mark which are yours. Act on one today. The rest stand where they are. Several can be true without being the one you move on. Moving on one is using what you know.
cells.sheetLine: The readings are yours, filed under circumstance.
cells.place: Where the road shows only its next step.
